questions.question: The phrase "if appropriate" is used in many places in the standard. How should a requirement carrying this qualifier be interpreted?

options.A: The requirement does not apply to the organization by default unless the customer agrees in writing
options.B: The requirement is considered applicable unless the organization can justify, with documented reasons, that it is not applicable
options.C: The auditor judges case by case, based on site conditions, whether the requirement applies to the organization
options.D: The requirement is considered applicable only when the risk assessment result is high risk

questions.explanation: Clause 1 states that a requirement carrying "if appropriate" is considered applicable unless the organization can document a justification that it is not; it is not a default exemption and requires neither customer agreement nor case-by-case auditor discretion.

questions.question: Under the standard's definitions, what is the key condition for deciding whether a material is a primary packaging material?

options.A: The material bears labeling information such as the drug name, batch number and expiry date
options.B: The material is used for outer protection and collective packing during drug transport
options.C: The material is manufactured and supplied by a supplier designated and approved by the pharmaceutical company
options.D: The material is used to contain, seal or dose a medicinal product and is in direct contact with it

questions.explanation: Clause 3.6.4 defines primary packaging material as a material used to contain, seal or dose that is in direct contact with the medicinal product. Cartons, labels, leaflets, outer packaging and shipping containers are non-contact secondary packaging materials, and whether a material is printed is not a criterion.

questions.question: A small packaging materials plant has a single quality head responsible for both QA and QC work. Under the definition of quality unit, is this arrangement acceptable?

options.A: Yes, the quality unit may be a single person or group
options.B: Yes, but another independent person must be assigned solely to QC and report directly to the customer
options.C: No, QA and QC must each be carried out by two separate organizational units
options.D: No, unless that head is also top management and signs all release documents

questions.explanation: Clause 3.1.2 defines the quality unit as the organizational unit fulfilling both QA and QC responsibilities; it may consist of separate QA and QC units, or be a single individual or group. One person holding both roles therefore does not violate the definition, and the claim that it "must be two separate organizational units" is wrong.

questions.question: An in-process control test shows that a process step is not yet complete, and the operator continues with the second part of that step. Under the definitions, which situation is this?

options.A: Reprocessing, which must first be agreed by the customer
options.B: Reconditioning, because the packaging material must be brought into compliance with specification
options.C: Part of the normal process, not considered reprocessing
options.D: Reprocessing, needing only a record in the batch record

questions.explanation: Reprocessing is repeating part of the process; however, when an IPC test shows that a part is incomplete, continuing to complete that part is considered normal processing and not reprocessing. Only true reprocessing and reconditioning require subsequent risk assessment and agreement with the customer.

questions.topic: Risk-based thinking applied to primary packaging
questions.question: What does clause 0.3.3 say about risk-based thinking in relation to the characteristics of primary packaging materials?

options.A: It needs to be applied only to a few critical processes such as design and development and sterilization
options.B: A risk-based approach is applied across all of the organization's processes
options.C: Risk assessment needs to be built into processes only when the customer requires it
options.D: It needs to be applied only to two processes: supplier evaluation and change control

questions.explanation: Clause 0.3.3 states explicitly that, because of the characteristics of primary packaging materials, the risk-based approach runs through all of the organization's processes, rather than being limited to a few critical processes or triggered only by customer requirements.

questions.question: According to 5.3, what does the standard specifically require of the quality unit responsible for quality critical decisions?

options.A: All quality critical decisions must be approved case by case by top management before being carried out
options.B: Quality critical decisions must be co-signed by the production head to ensure the decision is feasible
options.C: Decision authority must be separately delegated to the quality unit by the customer's representative in the contract
options.D: It must have the authority to make these decisions independently, free from influence by other departments

questions.explanation: Clause 5.3 requires that the quality unit responsible for quality critical decisions have the authority to make these decisions independently, which is the core GMP requirement for quality unit independence; requiring co-signature by the production head or case-by-case escalation to senior management would weaken this independence.

questions.question: According to 7.5.3.11, what is the minimum retention period for manufacturing, control, testing, distribution and investigation records?

options.A: At least five years from the date of manufacture of the packaging material, or as agreed with the customer
options.B: At least two years from the date of manufacture of the packaging material, or as agreed with the customer
options.C: At least five years from the date of batch release, or as agreed with the customer
options.D: At least five years from the date the customer receives the goods, or as agreed with the customer

questions.explanation: Clause 7.5.3.11 specifies that such records must be retained for at least five years from the date of manufacture of the packaging material, or as agreed with the customer; a note also reminds that retention to the end of the medicinal product's shelf life may be needed. Two years is the retention period for validation records after equipment decommissioning (8.5.1.2.3), which is easily confused.

questions.question: An operator enters a wrong value in a batch record. According to 7.5.3.6, which correction method is correct?

options.A: Cover the wrong value with correction fluid and rewrite it, with a confirming signature on the last page of the batch record
options.B: Erase the original value and enter the correct one, with the unit head adding a date and name on the same day
options.C: Strike through the value with a line and add the date and signature, with an explanation if necessary, keeping the original value legible
options.D: Rewrite the entire record on a new page and destroy the original page containing the error to avoid confusion

questions.explanation: Clause 7.5.3.6 requires corrections to be dated and signed or initialed, with an explanation where necessary, and the original entry must remain clearly legible. Correction fluid, erasing and destroying the original page all make the original record disappear.

questions.question: When primary packaging materials are exposed during production, how should they be handled according to 7.1.4.2.4?

options.A: They must always be handled in a classified clean zone, with no exceptions under any circumstances
options.B: They should be protected with covers, unless a documented risk assessment justifies not using them
options.C: A second person should witness throughout, unless the customer waives witnessing in writing
options.D: They should be cleaned at the end of each shift, unless the material is subsequently sterilized

questions.explanation: Clause 7.1.4.2.4 specifies that covers be used when packaging materials are exposed, unless a documented risk assessment justifies otherwise. It does not mandate operation in a clean zone and is unrelated to second-person witnessing or whether the material is later sterilized.

questions.question: During peak season, a packaging plant temporarily brings several agency workers onto the production line. According to 7.2.2.5, how should this be arranged?

options.A: Temporary personnel must be trained or work under the supervision of trained personnel
options.B: Temporary personnel may carry out general production work independently after reading and signing the SOP on their first day
options.C: Temporary personnel are limited to work that does not touch the product and are therefore exempt from training and supervision
options.D: Temporary personnel must first complete the annual GMP refresher cycle before entering the production area

questions.explanation: Clause 7.2.2.5 requires temporary personnel to be trained beforehand or to work under the supervision of trained personnel. Reading and signing an SOP is not training, and there is no need to wait until the whole annual refresher cycle is completed.

questions.question: When, for a quality critical material, the organization does not carry out full testing itself but accepts the supplier's CoA/CoC/CoT, what does the note in 8.4.2.2.10 require at a minimum?

options.A: Verification testing of half of the specification items for that material
options.B: Trend review of the supplier's last three CoAs, signed off by QA
options.C: The organization itself performing at least one specific identity test on the material or its subcomponent
options.D: Requiring the supplier to provide a copy of a CoA signed by an independent third-party laboratory

questions.explanation: Note 2 of 8.4.2.2.10 states that the organization may accept the supplier's CoA, CoC or CoT in place of its own testing, provided that the organization performs at least one specific identity test on the material or subcomponent. The standard does not require testing half of the items or third-party signature.

questions.question: A packaging materials plant plans to outsource sterilization to an external contractor. According to 8.4.2.2.2 and 8.4.2.2.7, which statement is correct?

options.A: It is enough to notify the customer after outsourcing is completed, and responsibility for sterilization passes to the contractor
options.B: The customer must be notified before outsourcing, and the outsourced sterilization process must comply with 8.5.1.2, 8.5.1.3 and 8.5.1.4
options.C: The customer need not be notified before outsourcing, as long as the contractor holds a valid certificate and validation documents are available
options.D: The customer must be notified beforehand, but the sterilization process need only comply with the sterilization-specific requirements of 8.5.1.4

questions.explanation: Clause 8.4.2.2.2 requires the customer to be notified before any part of the manufacturing process is outsourced; 8.4.2.2.7 requires the outsourced sterilization process to comply with 8.5.1.2 (validation), 8.5.1.3 (cleanliness and contamination control) and 8.5.1.4 (special requirements for sterile packaging materials), not just 8.5.1.4.

questions.question: Injection-molded thermoplastic packaging produces scrap, and the production unit wants to grind it and blend it back in. How should this be handled according to 8.5.1.3.11?

options.A: The organization may decide on its own, as long as the blend ratio is below an internally set limit and records are completed
options.B: It may be blended back in once the quality unit approves and line clearance is complete
options.C: It is always prohibited, because the standard does not allow any recycled material in packaging materials
options.D: Thermoplastic material must not be ground and reused unless agreed with the customer

questions.explanation: Clause 8.5.1.3.11 specifies that thermoplastic material must not be ground and reused in primary packaging materials unless agreed with the customer. It is not an absolute prohibition, but nor can the organization decide unilaterally; the parameters for reprocessed material must also be agreed with the customer (8.5.1.3.10).

questions.question: According to 8.5.1.2.3, how long should validation records be retained?

options.A: Throughout the period of use of the equipment and process, and for two further years after decommissioning, or as agreed with the customer
options.B: Five years from the date validation is completed, or extended to the end of the medicinal product's shelf life as agreed with the customer
options.C: Throughout the period of use of the equipment and process, and for five further years after decommissioning, or as agreed with the customer
options.D: Only until the next revalidation is completed, after which they may be destroyed under company internal procedures

questions.explanation: Clause 8.5.1.2.3 specifies that validation records be retained for the whole life cycle of the equipment and process and for two further years after decommissioning, or as agreed with the customer. Five years is the retention period for general manufacturing, testing and similar records (7.5.3.11); do not mix them up.

questions.question: According to 8.2.1.2.2, how should it be decided which changes need written confirmation before approval and which only need notification?

options.A: The organization's quality unit decides unilaterally under internal procedures and informs the customer at the annual review
options.B: Based on a fixed list in an annex to the standard, always treated as categories of change requiring written confirmation
options.C: The regulatory authority decides by product category, and the organization only follows it and notifies the customer afterwards
options.D: As required by the customer, the organization and customer agree on this together and communicate proposed changes in a timely manner

questions.explanation: Clause 8.2.1.2.2 specifies that, as required by the customer, the organization must agree with the customer which changes require written confirmation before approval and which only require notification, with proposed changes communicated in a timely manner, and recommends a documented technical/quality agreement. The standard provides no fixed list, and it is not decided unilaterally by the organization.

questions.question: A production line introduces an automated changeover system to shorten make-ready time but cannot achieve a full line clearance. According to 8.5.1.3.13, how should the organization handle this?

options.A: It must perform a documented risk assessment and operate with appropriate controls to ensure product quality
options.B: It must abandon the automated changeover system, because the standard requires full line clearance for all changeovers
options.C: It is enough to note partial clearance in the batch record, with no further assessment or control measures
options.D: It must obtain written customer approval and repeat full process validation after every changeover

questions.explanation: Clause 8.5.1.3.13 does not prohibit partial clearance or automated changeover, but requires that such systems have a documented risk assessment and operate with controls that ensure product quality. Merely noting it in the record without an assessment is not sufficient.

questions.question: According to 8.5.1.4.2, when should the sterilization process be validated if the packaging material needs to be sterilized?

options.A: After the first commercial batch ships, retrospectively together with customer complaint data
options.B: Only when a significant change occurs in the process or equipment
options.C: Before first use, and periodically revalidated thereafter
options.D: Before first use, and not revalidated afterwards as long as sterilization records are complete

questions.explanation: Clause 8.5.1.4.2 requires the sterilization process to be validated before first use and periodically revalidated, with the results recorded; ISO 11135, ISO 11137-1 or ISO 11137-2 may be consulted. Retrospective validation is not applicable to sterilization processes, and revalidating only on change is not enough.

questions.question: A plant recovers and reuses reusable packaging containers. According to 8.5.4.2.3, how should the containers be handled before reuse?

options.A: Only confirm that the container looks intact, and the original label may be kept to aid traceability of origin
options.B: Remove or obliterate the original label first, and clean the container, or verify it as clean, according to a documented procedure
options.C: Only the customer needs to confirm that the container is reusable, with no requirements on the original label or cleanliness status
options.D: Cover the original label with a new label, with the customer confirming container cleanliness before shipment

questions.explanation: Clause 8.5.4.2.3 specifies that reused packaging containers must first have previous labels removed or obliterated and be cleaned, or verified as clean, according to a documented procedure. Merely covering with a new label, or keeping the old one, can cause confusion and mix-up risk.

questions.question: After nonconforming product is produced, the organization proposes to release the batch anyway. According to 10.2.3 d), what condition must be met?

options.A: Approval signed by the quality unit and recorded in the batch record is enough to release
options.B: Approval signed by top management, ratified at the next management review
options.C: A risk assessment is completed and it is confirmed that the defect does not affect product appearance, after which the organization may release it itself
options.D: It must go through a documented concession, and that concession must be authorized by the customer

questions.explanation: Clause 10.2.3 d) specifies that any proposal to release nonconforming product must go through a documented concession authorized by the customer. Approval by the organization's own quality unit or top management cannot replace customer authorization.

questions.question: QC personnel take samples from the production line and send them to a separate testing laboratory, and the results are acceptable. According to 9.1.3.4.2, can these samples be returned to the production area?

options.A: Yes, as long as they are returned to the original batch and the quantity of samples is noted in the record
options.B: Yes, but only after written approval by the quality unit
options.C: No, samples that have been moved to a separate testing location must not be returned to the production area
options.D: No, unless the samples have been sterilized again and revalidated

questions.explanation: Clause 9.1.3.4.2 specifies that samples that have been moved to another testing location must not be returned to the production area; sampling for batch release (9.1.3.5) has the same requirement. Passing the test does not change this rule.

questions.question: According to Annex A.5, the 2015 edition no longer uses the term "exclusions". What precondition must be met when the organization determines that a requirement is not applicable?

options.A: The requirement is not in the product realization stage, and exclusion has been agreed by the customer in writing
options.B: The decision does not result in the organization's failure to achieve conformity of its products and services
options.C: The requirement is classified as optional, and the organization's size is below a certain headcount
options.D: The decision was passed at management review and approved and filed by an external certification body

questions.explanation: Annex A.5 and clause 4.3 explain that the organization may assess the applicability of requirements, but may decide a requirement is not applicable only if the decision does not result in failure to achieve conformity of its products and services, and the justification must be given in the documented scope of the QMS.

questions.question: According to A.6, how is the requirement for "records", which demonstrated conformity in ISO 9001:2008, expressed in the 2015 edition?

options.A: A requirement that the organization maintain documented information
options.B: A requirement that the organization establish a documented procedure
options.C: A requirement that the organization maintain a quality manual
options.D: A requirement that the organization retain documented information

questions.explanation: Annex A.6 explains that the former "documents", "documented procedures" and "quality manual" became "maintain documented information", while "records", used to show conformity, became "retain documented information". The two are not mutually exclusive, as the same information may need to be both maintained and retained.

questions.question: The 2015 edition has no separate "preventive action" clause. What reason does Annex A.4 give?

options.A: The QMS itself is a preventive tool, and the concept of prevention is expressed in the requirements through risk-based thinking
options.B: Preventive action has been fully replaced by the corrective action clause, and the organization no longer needs to take any preventive action
options.C: Preventive action is raised by the customer during audits, so the organization need not plan for it separately in its system
options.D: Preventive action is considered irrelevant to pharmaceutical GMP, so it is retained only in derivative standards for other industries

questions.explanation: Annex A.4 states that one of the main purposes of a QMS is to act as a preventive tool, so no separate preventive action clause is included and the concept of prevention is expressed through risk-based thinking. It also explains that 6.1 does not require a formal risk management method or a documented risk management process.

questions.question: A senior process engineer at a packaging plant is about to retire, and most of their experience has not been documented. Which risk to be guarded against in A.7, for organizational knowledge in 7.1.6, does this correspond to?

options.A: Decline in supplier capability, so that externally provided processes fail to meet requirements
options.B: Loss of document version control, so that operators use obsolete procedures
options.C: Loss of knowledge through staff turnover or failure to capture and share information
options.D: Changing customer needs, requiring existing product specifications to be renegotiated

questions.explanation: Annex A.7 states that one purpose of the organizational knowledge requirement is to avoid loss of knowledge, for example through staff turnover or failure to capture and share information; another is to encourage acquiring knowledge, such as by learning from experience, mentoring and benchmarking.

questions.question: According to Table B.1 of Annex B, which clause of this standard is ISO 10012 (guidelines for the management of measurement processes and measuring equipment) related to?

options.A: 7.2 Competence
options.B: 7.1.5 Monitoring and measuring resources
options.C: 9.2 Internal audit
options.D: 8.4 Control of externally provided processes, products and services

questions.explanation: Table B.1 maps ISO 10012 to 7.1.5 (monitoring and measuring resources); ISO 10015 maps to 7.2, ISO 19011 to 9.2 and ISO 10019 to 8.4. Annex B also states that the content of these documents does not add to or modify the requirements of this standard.

questions.question: Annex C lists gang printing (printing multiple designs on the same substrate in one production run) as an acute admixture risk. Under what condition may it be done according to C.2.5?

options.A: Only for different color versions of the same product for the same customer, with prior internal approval
options.B: Only during the make-ready stage, with all the mixed material segregated and scrapped after completion
options.C: As long as each design has an independent version number and start-up verification is completed, the organization may decide for itself
options.D: With customer agreement, after first completing a documented risk assessment to evaluate and reduce the risk of mix-ups

questions.explanation: Clause C.2.5 specifies that gang printing may be done only after obtaining customer agreement and completing a documented risk assessment to evaluate and reduce the risk of mix-ups and cross-contamination. Version numbers and start-up verification alone cannot replace customer agreement.

questions.question: According to C.2.1.1, what kind of material should be used for the initial print make-ready of a printing press?

options.A: Finished conforming printed product, to ensure color and registration match the customer's proof
options.B: Unprinted components or materials, and not material that has already been printed
options.C: Printed material left over from the previous work order, to reduce material waste and cost
options.D: Sample print sheets supplied by the customer, released together with the batch after adjustment

questions.explanation: Clause C.2.1.1 specifies that initial make-ready must use unprinted components or materials. C.2.1.4 further specifies that material used for make-ready be segregated and disposed of as production waste, so that printed items do not get mixed into the production batch.

questions.question: D.3.2.1 states that prospective validation is preferred and that concurrent or retrospective validation may be accepted in specific circumstances. What limitation does this exception have for sterilization processes?

options.A: Sterilization processes may use concurrent validation but not retrospective validation
options.B: Sterilization processes may use retrospective validation, but customer written agreement must be obtained
options.C: The exception does not apply to sterilization processes, which may use neither concurrent nor retrospective validation
options.D: Sterilization processes are the same as other processes, and any of the three approaches may be chosen depending on the risk assessment result

questions.explanation: Clause D.3.2.1 states explicitly that the acceptance of concurrent or retrospective validation does not apply to sterilization processes (see 8.5.1.4.2); sterilization processes must be validated before first use.

questions.question: A packaging plant has a piece of inspection equipment that generates data and records used for "accept or reject" decisions but does not directly contact the product. How should it be handled according to D.3.4?

options.A: Treat it as critical equipment, subject to verification/qualification and included in the VMP
options.B: Treat it as non-critical, managed under good engineering practices, and not included in the VMP
options.C: Handle it first by retrospective validation, and decide afterwards whether to include it in the VMP
options.D: Treat it as critical equipment, but perform qualification only after the customer requests it

questions.explanation: In the decision questions of D.3.4, a "yes" answer to any of them (including whether the equipment produces data or records used for accept or reject decisions) makes the equipment critical; critical equipment should be subject to verification or qualification and included in the validation master plan. Not directly contacting the product does not make it non-critical.

questions.topic: Replacement print plates during a run
questions.question: A print plate is damaged during a print run and must be replaced. If the new plate is made from an existing, approved fixed source (such as existing film or an existing stepped image for computer-to-plate), how should it be handled according to C.2.4?

options.A: Always stop the job and treat it as a new batch, with all replacement plates treated as a new origination
options.B: The job may continue after a new "first off" check is completed; if the source is a new source, it must be treated as a new origination and a new batch started
options.C: The job may continue after start-up verification is completed, and it need not be treated as a new batch regardless of the plate source
options.D: All material already printed must first be destroyed, and the job restarted from the beginning after the customer confirms the new plate

questions.explanation: Clause C.2.4.1 specifies that for replacement plates from an existing approved fixed source, the job may continue after a new first off check; C.2.4.2 specifies that if the plate is made from a new source (such as a re-stepped one-up image), the job must be stopped, the replacement plate treated as a new origination, and subsequent production treated as a new batch; the introduction of all replacement plates must be recorded.
